newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- When meeting U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, Chinese President Jiang Zemin urged the development of a constructive and cooperative relationship between China and the United States.
-- Shanghai aims to reach a per capita residential area of 10 square metres by the end of the century.

-- EXPRESS DAILY -- A member of the Democratic Party, Chan Choi-hi, announced that he would apply for a seat on the provisional legislature. More members of the party are expected to change their stance towards the provisional legislature.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Orient Overseas (Internatinal) Ltd was in discussion with the Shanghai municipal government over two residential development projects. An agreement was expected to be reached in three mnnths' time.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Market sources said the family of Robert Kwok sold 15 million shares in Citic Pacific through Morgan Stanley, at $39.2 per share.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Figures compiled by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority showed that growth in residential mortgage lending rose dramatically last month, underlining the continuing property boom in the territory which has pushed the stock market to a series of new highs in recent weeks.
-- Stock exchange Chairman Edgar Cheng said laws on market manipulation did not need to be revised, despite calls to make it easier to prove such activity has taken place.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD --Experts say that demand for tighter liquidity as the end of the year approaches and a bull run on China's stock markets will depress the price of the country's first seven-year government bond to be listed today.
-- The Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum was nearing a consensus on a United States proposal to free information technology trade, without the participation of Taiwan and China.
